items.title: Beyond Scalar Leaderboards: Adaptive Sampling for Pareto Frontier Identification in Multi-Objective LLM Arenas
items.why: Proposes adaptive sampling for Pareto-frontier identification in multi-objective LLM arenas, a new statistical method for more sample-efficient leaderboard evaluation beyond scalar Elo scores.

items.title: Adversarial Benchmarks and BenchDoor Attacks: Exploiting Benchmark Incentives for Backdoor Attacks
items.why: Introduces BenchDoor, data-poisoning attacks that exploit benchmark-driven training incentives to implant backdoors, directly relevant to benchmark gaming and reward hacking concerns.

items.title: ABench: Adversarily Benchmarking Large Language Models across Taxonomized Values
items.why: Presents an adversarial, taxonomized benchmark for testing LLM robustness across cultural values beyond English-centric discriminative tests, a new alignment eval method.

items.title: The Instruction Tax on Factual Recall: Base Models Can Beat Their Instruction-Tuned Counterparts
items.why: Shows base models can outperform instruction-tuned counterparts on a factual-recall knowledge-base completion task, a concrete finding about instruction-tuning costs relevant to eval design and prompting methodology.

items.title: Rewards for Budget-Aware Multi-Turn Agents That Adapt to Arbitrary Test-Time Constraints
items.why: Studies whether multi-turn LLM agents can learn to allocate a given inference budget across turns via RL, directly relevant to reward design and agent evaluation under constraints.

items.title: The Reward Model Selection Crisis in Personalized Alignment
items.why: Identifies a mismatch between personalized reward model accuracy and actual downstream behavior under inference-time reward-guided decoding, directly relevant to reward modeling and reward hacking concerns.

items.title: Agents-as-Peers: Bias-Controlled LLM Evaluation as Multi-Agent Peer Assessment
items.why: Proposes a distributed multi-agent peer-assessment protocol as an alternative to fixed benchmarks or centralized LLM judges, a new eval methodology addressing judge bias and benchmark contamination.

items.title: Do LMs Know What Variables Do? Interpreting Code Representations via Variable Roles
items.why: Uses SAEs to test whether variable-role concepts (accumulator, traversal, etc.) are linearly recoverable and controllable in code LLMs, a concrete mech-interp probe on a non-toy domain.

items.title: Ask Less, Ask Better: Allocating User Attention in Proactive LLM Agents with Interruption Budgets
items.why: Proposes an interruption-budget evaluation protocol that separates question frequency from question quality for proactive agents, a reusable eval method for human-AI interaction research.

items.title: From Stories to Features: Scaling Concept Vectors for AI Alignment & Interpretability
items.why: Introduces a targeted, scalable method for extracting safety-relevant concept vectors (honesty, deception) as an alternative to full SAE feature extraction, directly relevant to alignment/interp work.

items.title: Beyond Factual Accuracy: A Benchmark for Evaluating Perspective Alignment in LLMs
items.why: Introduces PerspectiveBench, a new benchmark isolating perspective-alignment failures that standard factuality metrics miss, a novel eval axis adoptable for LLM evaluation research.

items.title: No Matter Who You Are: Addressivity and Sycophancy in Large Language Models
items.why: Mechanistically investigates how post-training's addressee-directed framing causally produces sycophantic behavior, linking interpretability to a known reward-hacking-adjacent failure mode.

items.title: CALM: Consistency-Aware Logit Masking in Decoding Space for Mitigating Overthinking of Large Reasoning Models
items.why: Proposes a logit-masking decoding method to reduce overthinking in reasoning models using consistency signals rather than naive truncation, relevant to reasoning-model efficiency/behavior evaluation.

items.title: LEAPS: Long-context Evaluation of Adaptive Pattern Learning and State Tracking
items.why: LEAPS is a new long-context benchmark decomposing recall, state tracking, and pattern learning for agentic long-trajectory use cases, a reusable eval harness.

items.title: HarnessRL: Co-Evolving Policies with a Just-in-Time Training Harness for Open-Ended RL
items.why: Identifies concrete failure modes (reward collapse, spurious rewards) in rubric-based RL and proposes a co-evolving training harness, directly relevant to reward hacking research.

items.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Preference Reward Models with Evolving Penalties
items.why: Proposes evolving penalty methods to curb reward hacking in preference reward models used in RLHF, directly on-topic for reward hacking research.

items.title: HoloCosm: Beyond Single-Metric Benchmark Compression Across Multiple Metrics
items.why: New benchmark-compression method that accounts for weak correlation across multiple evaluation metrics, useful for researchers building cheaper eval harnesses.

items.title: The Judge Can Debias Itself: Awareness and Self-Debiasing for Reliable LLM-as-a-Judge
items.why: Introduces lightweight bias-aware prompting and self-debiasing strategies to improve LLM-as-a-Judge reliability, directly useful for eval harness design.

items.title: Pluralistic Alignment in Language Models: Objectives, Human References, and Preference Representations
items.why: Offers a taxonomy disentangling objectives, reference populations, and evidence standards for pluralistic alignment, relevant to human-AI interaction and preference-based evaluation design.

items.title: Medical Fine-Tuning Reshapes, Not Reduces, Patient-Facing AI Risk: A Rubric-Based, LLM-Judge Evaluation Framework
items.why: Introduces a risk-sensitive, rubric-based LLM-judge evaluation framework showing that medical fine-tuning changes rather than eliminates patient-facing harm risk, a new eval method beyond factuality scoring.

items.title: SoK: PIAtlas: Decomposing the Unbounded Prompt Injection Attack Space
items.why: Systematizes 20+ incompatible prompt injection datasets into a unified taxonomy (PIAtlas), useful as a reference structure for building or comparing red-teaming/eval benchmarks.

items.title: Policy Is Not Capability: Some Safety Benchmarks Measure Which Definition of "Unsafe" You Trained On
items.why: Uses a real industrial dataset labeled under two different policy definitions to show guardrail/safety benchmark scores reflect training-label policy rather than an objective 'unsafe' property, a methodological critique relevant to eval validity.

items.title: VibeTraining-Bench: Data-Trainer-Harness Co-Design for Iterative System Improvement
items.why: New benchmark (VibeTraining-Bench) specifically testing agents' ability to co-design data/trainer/inference harness for recursive self-improvement, directly relevant to RL training and agentic capability eval.

items.title: Strength Controls Change How Interventions Compare Across Sparse Autoencoder Codes
items.why: Mechanistic interpretability paper showing that strength-matching controls (norm vs output calibration) change conclusions when comparing SAE code interventions, relevant to rigor in interp methodology.

items.title: RouterWorld: Scaling Conversational AI with Latency-Aware LLM Routing
items.why: Introduces RouterWorld, a new LLM-routing benchmark addressing latency as a first-class metric and realistic partial-observability settings, a concrete eval harness improvement over existing routing benchmarks.

items.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
items.why: New benchmark (SpatialScout) testing whether VLM agents can actively explore and build metric 3D maps, going beyond static spatial QA.

items.title: PaperAudit-Bench: Benchmarking Error Detection in Research Papers for Critical Automated Peer Review
items.why: New benchmark (PaperAudit-Bench) with 220 papers and 2,200+ synthetic errors for testing LLM error detection in automated peer review, adoptable for scientific-reasoning eval.

items.title: 'Your AI Text is not Mine': Redefining and Evaluating AI-generated Text Detection under Realistic Assumptions
items.why: Proposes a reframed, more realistic definition and evaluation protocol for AI-generated text detection, challenging existing dataset/benchmark assumptions in the field.

items.title: EvoBrowseComp: Benchmarking Search Agents on Evolving Knowledge
items.why: New dynamic benchmark (EvoBrowseComp) targeting search-agent evaluation on evolving knowledge to counter contamination issues in static benchmarks like BrowseComp.

items.title: Open-sci-ref-0.02: open reference baselines for reproducible language model and dataset comparison
items.why: Releases open reference baseline models/training runs at multiple scales to enable reproducible comparison of LM architectures and datasets, useful infrastructure for eval researchers.

items.title: Bayesian Preference Learning for Test-Time Steerable Reward Models
items.why: Proposes a Bayesian reward-model approach enabling test-time steerability of preferences, directly relevant to RL alignment and reward modeling research.

items.title: Superficial Success vs. Internal Breakdown: An Empirical Study of Generalization in Adaptive Multi-Agent Systems
items.why: Empirical study showing multi-agent LLM systems overfit to specific task topologies and exhibit internal reasoning breakdown despite surface-level success, relevant to evaluating agentic system generalization.
